title: Chain-tip citations stay unpinned even after P32.13 deploys: BaseLayout never passes a release to Citation, so every site page keeps the 'Belief-pinned permalink (reproducible after SIG corrects itself)' query-string URL, and the only as-of selector resolver is an offline CLI with no serving route
evidence: BaseLayout.astro:129 renders <Citation path={path} title={title} asOf={asOf} rulesetVersion={rulesetVersion} /> with no release prop (the only <Citation usage in web/src, grep). Citation.astro renders the release-permalink branch only when Astro.props.release is set; otherwise line 60 prints 'Belief-pinned permalink (reproducible after SIG corrects itself)' with the ?as_of_world=&as_of_belief=&ruleset= URL. The resolver for those parameters, release.resolve_selector (release.py:1553), is reachable only via `sig-exports release resolve` (cli.py:1265-1272); ops/web/nginx.conf has locations /r/, /releases/, /entity/ and the withdrawn_*.conf include (lines 117-143) but no handling of selector query strings, so a static origin keeps serving current bytes for any selector. Consequence (inference): deploying P32.13 (G2 step 7, ACT-24) pins only /r/<pub>/ record and dossier routes; every Astro page (home, dossiers, methodology, coverage, freshness) keeps the false reproducibility claim that C2 NEW-4 / J1 NEW-5 observed live. SIG-FIND-002: 'an ignored query string cannot masquerade as an as-of answer'. Tree identical to chain tip b051732c for these paths.

title: The P32.2 actual-capture writer hard-codes storage_tier='public' and /v1/evidence serves source_uri for every tier with bytes_available derived from that tier, so once L44-52 go live captures of derived-only, restricted and Part VIII sources will be advertised as public downloads with raw upstream URLs (latent)
evidence: _INSERT_OCCURRENCE (claim_sink.py:573-580) inserts every actual capture with the literal storage_tier 'public' (line 579: VALUES (..., 'public', ...)); the actual artifact insert (_ACTUAL_ARTIFACT) leaves evidence_artifact.sensitivity_tier at its DEFAULT 0 (evidence.sql:28) and sets url = source_uri. PgReadStore.capture (store_pg.py:777-795) returns ec.source_uri and ec.storage_tier; tiers.public_representation (tiers.py:62-83) always includes source_uri and sets bytes_available = tier.bytes_are_public (true for 'public'); SEALED_PUBLIC_FIELDS (tiers.py:93-105) also includes source_uri. No code derives the tier from the source's redistribution lane or Part VIII class, and no S-1/S-6 URL scrub exists on this path (J4 §8). J4 classes 172 in-scope sources derived-only and 10 restricted (e.g. eyes_on_flock, P8-1 search reasons; agency_audit_export). Latent: the actual-capture path needs sqitch L44 (claim_assertion_bindings), undeployed on hosted (G2 §1, step 1). Relates to but differs from J1 NEW-4 (the synthetic capture) and J1 NEW-9 (blanket grant).

title: Freshness 'last content change' is the last run that inserted at least one claim, not an upstream content change; the capture digests that would measure change are unused
evidence: SOURCE_COMPLETIONS_QUERY (shaping.py:1597-1602): 'max(finished_at) FILTER (WHERE claims_inserted > 0) AS last_content_change'. A run whose upstream content changed only by deletions (disappearances) or whose changed bytes yield only duplicate claims never moves the date; a claim-inserting run caused by SIG-side changes moves it without any upstream change (inference). ingest_run_capture records capture_digest per target per execution (ingest_run_capture.sql:32-47), which is the direct change signal Transitland/OpenSanctions use (J2 PC-2), but no export reads it. The public column is labelled 'Last content change' (SIG-METRIC-007 requires 'last content change').

title: Historical selectors and the release compatibility index are date-granular, so two releases activated on one day with the same ruleset make every legacy citation for that day 'ambiguous' (409)
evidence: _update_compat (release.py:1025-1049) stores as_of_world/as_of_belief from the manifest's as_of_snapshot/as_of_belief (dates, per descriptor_document :166-206); _normalise_selector (:1534-1550) collapses an ISO instant to its UTC date; resolve_selector (:1553-1629) returns {'status':'ambiguous'} when more than one activated publication matches. Citations minted by the site carry only the date pair and ruleset (Citation.astro), so a same-day correction republish (likely in Round-11's honesty and attribution waves, G2 steps 0c/0d) would turn every citation for that date into a 409 once the resolver is served (inference). Needs a rule (one activation per date+ruleset) or a release-scoped selector parameter.
